claims.text: Adding a controlled amount of carbon during synthesis will improve both glass-forming ability and amorphous-state thermal stability in phosphorus-containing high-entropy alloys.
The undoped phosphorus-containing high-entropy alloy has modest glass-forming ability under rapid cooling.
The undoped phosphorus-containing high-entropy alloy has limited thermal stability.
An organic medium or carbon-containing precursor can supply active carbon that may be incorporated as a dopant during laser synthesis of compositionally complex alloys.
Pulsed laser ablation in liquid can provide high cooling rates and kinetic control over nanoparticle structural formation.
Rapid solidification is a condition under which the proposed carbon intervention should improve the phosphorus-containing alloy.
Processing temperatures must avoid unwanted carbide formation for the intervention to be beneficial.
Carbon dopants will segregate at interfaces in the phosphorus-containing alloy.
Carbon can form thin carbon-rich regions or shells in laser-fabricated compositionally complex alloy particles.
Interfacial or carbon-rich regions will hinder atomic mobility.
Carbon doping will increase local structural disorder in the phosphorus-containing alloy.
Carbon doping will disrupt atomic bonding in the phosphorus-containing alloy.
The carbon-induced structural changes will retard crystalline nucleation and growth.
Retarding crystalline nucleation and growth will promote amorphization and stabilize the amorphous state.
The carbon-doped alloy will have a larger critical casting diameter than the undoped baseline.
The carbon-doped alloy will require a lower critical cooling rate than the undoped baseline.
The carbon-doped alloy will have a higher crystallization-onset temperature than the undoped baseline.
The beneficial effect will occur only within an optimized carbon-concentration range.
Excessive carbon may produce carbides or other deleterious phases.
The magnitude of improvement may depend on processing conditions and alloy composition.

contradictions.description: The experiment states that composition should be identical across the carbon-doped and undoped sets, but adding carbon necessarily changes composition. The intended control can match the underlying alloy composition and all processing parameters, but not total elemental composition.
